record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a truncated file list only; code and result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports difference-in-means direction analyses, layer-wise causal patching, and steering outcomes across post-training settings, but does not report the original all-layer direction ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The README reports qualitative direction-geometry and causal-patching findings, plus steering effects on MMLU. It does not give numerical results for the refusal-direction and patching figures. File names in the list are not treated as results. The stated 31.6% XSTest over-refusal result is recorded as a finding outside the listed versions; it is not evidence about adding or removing the difference-in-means direction.
record.test_reason: The README uses difference-in-means refusal-direction extraction, activation patching and ActAdd/ITI steering to compare SFT, Ra-SFT and ORPO checkpoints. It reports only qualitative summaries: per-layer direction magnitude and geometry shifts, per-layer patching profiles, an MMLU drop under steering, and one XSTest over-refusal number. It reports no refusal rate after ablating or adding the direction. It does not test whether a single removable direction exists under each objective. None of these results measures what V1 or V7 names, so no version is tested on the available text. The full paper (arXiv 2609.03887) and the result files may contain such tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the post-training objective reshapes refusal-direction geometry and the layers causally responsible for refusal. Ra-SFT spreads computation across layers while SFT/ORPO show a mid-to-late peak. They argue that no offline objective satisfies all three trilemma properties: distributed encoding, safety/utility separability and granular correctability. Ra-SFT is the most correctable, ORPO gives the largest ASR reductions but the worst over-refusal, Llama's steering costs MMLU, and Gemma's redundant encoding resists targeted correction.
record.recipe_differences: Research pipeline for comparing post-training objectives using difference-in-means refusal-direction extraction, causal patching, steering, and safety/utility benchmarks; the README does not claim to reproduce the original study's intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports different refusal-direction geometry and causal layer profiles by training objective; it also reports an MMLU cost for Llama under small-strength ActAdd steering.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-training shifts each objective's refusal direction away from the base model and from the other objectives. Ra-SFT is the outlier and SFT/ORPO stay closer together, across Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B and Qwen3-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training objective changes the per-layer geometry of the difference-in-means refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation patching shows refusal computation distributed gradually across layers under Ra-SFT. Under SFT/ORPO it is concentrated in a mid-to-late-layer peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-chain supervision spreads refusal-relevant computation across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama, ActAdd steering toward safety collapses MMLU accuracy at small steering strengths. No values or checkpoint are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety steering vectors can carry a large general-capability cost when safety and utility representations overlap.
Preference-based post-training can produce substantial over-refusal on benign prompts.

record.peer_reviewed: EMNLP 2026 Main Conference (as stated in the README)
record.problems: The available README summary gives no numerical values or uncertainty for the direction-geometry and patching findings. The listed result files were not read, and the README does not specify the checkpoint behind the Llama MMLU statement.
record.rows_left_out: No results were extracted from named files in the file list. The README refers to Figures 2–3, but the supplied text gives only qualitative summaries, so figure-only numerical results were not recorded.

untested.parts: No refusal rate after ablating the direction, and none after adding it. Capability preservation under direction ablation is also not reported in the README.
Whether each objective (SFT, Ra-SFT, ORPO) yields one removable refusal direction. Only geometry and patching profiles are described.
Ra-SFT trains reasoning traces, but the README gives no direction-ablation result for reasoning models.

missing.what: ActAdd steering refusal/ASR results on WildJailbreak at positive and negative alpha for each checkpoint. These may show whether adding or subtracting a refusal vector changes refusal rates, if the vector is the difference-in-means direction.
Refusal-direction extraction results per model and objective, including candidate-layer magnitudes and any ablation or selection scores.
The full paper's Sections 4.3–4.4 and steering sections. These may report direction ablation or addition effects and MMLU numbers.
XSTest over-refusal under negative ActAdd steering for Gemma ORPO.

record.verdict_notes: The verdict rests on the README only. The repository holds many result files (steering ASR at multiple alphas, direction results) that could convert this into a V1/V7 test if they report refusal rates under direction addition or subtraction. The reader's 'challenges' label for V1 from R4 is dropped: ActAdd is not shown to use the difference-in-means direction, and no refusal rate is given. The 'supports' label for V7 is dropped: geometry differences do not address whether a single removable direction exists.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report ablating the extracted direction at every layer and position, nor a refusal rate after removing it or adding it. The MMLU result bears only on the capability-preservation part.
No weight-edit or abliteration result is reported in the README.
The README does not report attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
The README does not test an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
The README does not compare harmfulness judgments with refusal decisions.
Comparisons across architectures are reported, but not transfer across languages, model variants sharing a base, or base-to-instruct models.

The README compares post-training objectives and reports changes in refusal-direction geometry and layer-wise causal effects, but does not establish whether a single direction is removable under each objective or when during training it becomes removable.
The README includes reasoning-aware SFT as a training objective, but does not report a test of the claim in models that reason before answering.
